value.body: A farm manager runs the daily work of a farm — planning crops, supervising workers, managing irrigation and inputs, and keeping records. Corporate farms, plantations, polyhouse and hydroponic units, agri start-ups and large landholders hire them. Some graduates manage their own family farms in the same way.

items.label: Work setting
items.value: On-site at the farm, often in rural or peri-urban areas

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually start as a farm supervisor or assistant manager in a commercial farm, plantation or protected-cultivation unit, and take on full responsibility with experience.

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: senior farm manager, operations head, or running one's own farm or agri venture.
Weather and market prices affect the job heavily.
Experience here is useful for starting an agri-business later.

value.title: B.Agri enrolment in India
value.note: Counts students across all years of the B.Agri programme, not farm-manager jobs. Programmes reported under other names (such as B.Sc Agriculture) may be counted elsewhere.

competition.note: B.Sc Agriculture (B.Agri) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among B.Sc Agriculture (B.Agri) graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
women.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
